articleTitle: Towards Real Time Vehicle Counting using YOLO-Tiny and Fast Motion Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Real-time vehicle detection, tracking and counting from surveillance cameras is a main part for many applications in smart cities. Usually, this task encounters some problems in practice, like the lack of real-time processing of the videos or the errors in detection and/or tracking. In this paper we propose an approach for real time vehicle counting by using Tiny YOLO for detection and fast motion estimation for tracking. Our application is running in Ubuntu with GPU processing, and the next step is to test it on low-budget devices, as Jetson Nano. Experimental results show that our approach achieves high accuracy at real time speed (33.5 FPS) on real traffic videos.

articleTitle: LoRaWAN Gateway: Design, Implementation and Testing in Real Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The interest in developing systems working with IoT platforms is increasing nowadays. Thus, many smart sensors can communicate over the Internet without human mediation using LPWAN networks. This paper presents a low-cost high-performance multi-channel Gateway for LoRaWAN technology. In order to validate the Gateway performances, the TTN cloud data network it’s used. The configuration of the Gateway consists of a Raspberry Pi 3B+ and an iC880A concentrator LoRa Gateway board. The Gateway is certified by LoRaWAN Alliance and supports multichannel communication. Also, the system integrates a 2.2 dBi Omnidirectional antenna. From the performed measurements, the Gateway ensures a high level of performance and a maximum communication distance of 2.5 km in rural areas, and 1.3 km in urban areas with a PER of less than 20%.

articleTitle: Opportunities of using artificial intelligence in hardware verification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Over the last decade, usage of integrated circuits met an unprecedently spread in most domains of human activity. Processors are embedded in more and more products, consequently, request for their manufacturing increased exponentially. Since hardware verification is a very time-consuming step in electronics development, engineers make huge efforts to reduce its time by increasing automation of this process, and artificial intelligence is an ideal candidate for that job. Aligning to this global effort, advanced methods for improving verification performance are analyzed in this paper. Current research represents an important step before proceeding to implementation of artificial intelligence concepts inside integrated circuit verification process. Machine learning in verification can be used for multiple directions: generating code for driving full range of stimuli needed to bring verified circuit into all its functional states; analyzing test results; filling coverage gaps and list of examples can highly continue. However, a big challenge is to decide which parts of verification environment can best address needs of automation and which verification techniques are most suitable for supplying data to automatic code generators. In this article, some features of e language are highlighted as welcome bridges between hardware verification and artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Reliability Calculation Method for Output Capacitor Bank used in Telecom Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper evaluates reliability of a power supply. For a telecom power supply, the capacitor bank accounts for the most of the failure rate. A complete calculation is provided herein based on IEC TR 62380 standard. This is a reliability data handbook for prediction on electronics components, PCBs and equipment, which has the advantage of taking directly into account the influence of the environment with calculation models. Thus, thermal cycling seen by components is function of equipment mission profile and replaces previously used environment factor, often having a difficult evaluation. Finally, the paper compares results from calculation with MIL-HDBK217 and IEC TR 62380.

articleTitle: Preventing the Temperature Side Channel Attacks on Security Circuits
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Security circuits are important parts of communication and data processing equipment. Nowadays technologies and computation power can be used in cryptanalytic attacks against these specialized pieces of equipment. Some collateral procedures have been developed to facilitate these attacks and they are called Side Channel Attacks. They force the physical limits of the logic circuits in order to provoke erroneous operations that will later help the cryptanalytic attacks. One of the most used side channel attack consists in forcing the security circuit to work at temperatures out of the operating limits or to quickly freeze it. Freezing at very low temperatures can block processors and memories with resident secret data stored in them. Later on, these data can be acquired and used in cryptanalytic attacks. This paper proposes a special conductive mesh that can act also as a temperature sensor. Besides its function to detect physical intrusions, its behavior at temperature variations makes it a very good detector of temperature side channel attacks. Considering that the conductive mesh is covering the security circuit, the active tamper detection circuit, which probes with signals and analyze the response of the conductive mesh, is capable of detecting more quickly the temperature variations than a temperature sensor located at the circuit board.

articleTitle: IoT Solution for Plant Monitoring in Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) current solutions involving Cloud Computing facilities in the agricultural domain can provide different information on diseases and plant development during the phonological cycle. These solutions are needed to monitor drought, plant diseases, and plant growth and to enable the possibility to discover personalized solutions depending on the monitored parameters. This paper aims to illustrate how, using an IoT ADCON-based station for plant monitoring (grapevine), important sensor-collected data can be extracted and interpreted (e.g. variation of leaf wetness, soil and air humidity, air and soil temperature). Based on these values automatic or human decisions can be made in order to improve productivity in terms of grapes quality. The main advantages of the presented solution consist of solar panel supply and data reliability ensuring thus a power-efficient and productive agricultural process.

articleTitle: A New Pupil Detection Algorithm Based on Circular Hough Transform Approaches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper a new pupil detection algorithm based on circular Hough transform approaches is presented. The proposed algorithm includes an adaptive quantitative binarization procedure, a pupil reconstruction stage by using certain morphological operations and the image contour detection performed with the Laplace operator. To save the computing resources, the circular Hough transform is applied on the edge of the binarized eye image and provides better results for noisy eye image captured in nonuniform and variable lighting conditions. The CHT based algorithm achieves a detection rate at five pixels higher than 82% for three different and highly representative databases, totalizing 1324 eye images.

articleTitle: Automated Thermal Images Processing System for Change Detection and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A thermal image processing system (TIPS) is developed for change detection and diagnosis (CDD) purposes, in general, and for electronic circuits with electric power components and devices, in particular. The task of the system is to perform CDD based on automatic thermal image processing, by using Matlab environment as support of development. The system contains specialized libraries, organized as toolboxes. Two main categories of functions could be considered. The first one contains basic and advanced functions for thermal image processing. Some of them are original, such as the functions for modeling of the evolution of the temperature. The second category contains functions for CDD based on machine learning paradigm, especially for neural computation. Experiments made on power supplying circuits for general computers show the fezability of the solution and reveals some advantages of this solution as flexibility, simplicity and easy to understand and to integrate other classical or advanced processing functions.

articleTitle: Metrological Assessment of an Electronic System for Monitoring the Geometrical Parameters of Cylindrical Profiles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: To manage the quality of finished mill products, an electronic system for monitoring the geometrical parameters of cylindrical profiles was developed at the University of Ruse "Angel Kanchev". The aim of the electronic system is every cylindrical profile to be accompanied by a certificate of quality. Experimental researches have been conducted to evaluate the metrological accuracy class of the eight linear optoelectronic converters which are used as sensors. The intrinsic measurement error of the linear optoelectronic converters, define the accuracy class of the developed electronic system.

articleTitle: Extended Current Range of Active Balancing and Monitoring Circuits for Supercapacitor Modules
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The present paper continues our investigations in the field of Supercapacitors or Electrochemical Double Layer Capacitors, briefly named EDLCs [1]. During charging process EDLCs modules experience uneven state of charge (SOC) caused by manufacturing dispersions. Hence, the need for supplemental circuits to monitor and balance the charging process. The complex circuit for charging, monitoring and balancing presented in [1] has proven its effectiveness, but was limited to maximum charge/discharge currents of 500mA and a total capacitance of 4.4 F. We propose in the paper a modification of the power components in the circuit to permit a charge/discharge with 2A maximum current, that will permit us to handle a total capacitance of 40F, that corresponds to an individual capacitance of 200F. We will present the complete circuit, electrical simulation for major sub-circuits involved in charging/discharging and measurement of charge/discharge cycles.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Micrometric Magnetoresistive Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the design and characterization of multilayered spin valve structures to be used as magnetic field sensor. To enhance the performance of the sensor and to reduce the density of magnetic domain formation, two geometries of the magnetoresistive element are investigated. A meander structure element and a yoke configuration are designed with different parameters such as the width of the stripe (4 μm ÷ 8 μm), length and number of segments on a 10 mm x 20 mm mask. UV photolithography is used for micrometric patterning of the geometric shapes. The response of the as obtained devices is characterized in terms of the magnetoresistive ratio by measuring the variation curves of the electrical resistance when applying an external magnetic field.

articleTitle: Pests detection system for agricultural crops using intelligent image analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper proposes an intelligent method for real-time monitoring of the evolution of pests in an agricultural crop. The system consists of a pheromone trap, a camera that periodically fetches frames with trap and a data transceiver module where the frame is encapsulated with the date and station id. The data arrives at a server where they are retrieved and analyzed using two deep learning artificial neural networks. One determines the type and number of pests and the other identifies the evolution of the pest population. The system has been experimented with an apple tree culture in order to early identify pests and combat them.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic energy harvester
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Energy harvesting is the technology which gathers and converts external energies such as light, vibration and heat which are disposed into reusable electrical energy and uses such electrical energy. The vibration energy harvesting is very interesting technology because it produces very high density of energy and unaffected by the climate.This paper presents an approach to linear magnetic generators for use in environments that present high amplitude, low frequency vibrations. A prototype has been developed and several efficiency improvement ideas have been investigated. Experimental vibration shaker test is conducted to assess the performance of the energy harvester.

articleTitle: Protecting the Secrets: Advanced Technique for Active Tamper Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Cryptographic modules and security circuits are the kernels of every piece of equipment that process security data. No matter where they are deployed, the equipment must be protected against physical attacks, as no one can access the electronic circuits that process the security data: firmware implementations, cryptographic keys and secret data. The most effective way to protect this kind of electronic circuits is to wrap them in a special conductive mesh and probe it with proper signals in order to detect intrusions. This paper provides a complete solution for intrusions detection: a system made of a special conductive mesh and an active tamper detection circuit. The conductive mesh consists of three layers that detect intrusions earlier than the effective penetration of the mesh. The active tamper detection circuit is designed to probe the mesh with signals that cannot be emulated by an adversary.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Powered LoRa-based IoT Multi Sensor Node
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: LPWAN systems and low power sensors are used nowadays in many applications where long-range communications at a low bit-rate are required. This paper presents a photovoltaic panel powered IoT multi sensor using LoRa technology for data transmission. This type of sensor is intended to be mounted in outside isolated areas and can transmit data once a day when the required power for the transmitter (in this case LoRaWAN module) is enough. Moreover, information can be obtained from surfaces that can cover areas of tens of square kilometers without human intervention. Given these conditions, the replacement of a conventional sensor battery may become a major or not even a feasible issue due to the high costs that can be more than the sensor itself. The experimental results show that using only a single photovoltaic panel, the node can communicate with the LoRaWAN Gateway without any issues.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison of Conducted Emissions in Automotive EMC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Interlaboratory comparison is performed to ensure repeatability amongst EMC laboratories worldwide regarding specific test methods. The purpose of this paper is to present two interlaboratory comparison methods (CE-LISN and CE-current probe) for conducted emissions (CE) testing used by 6 laboratories. A statistical analysis method is applied, based on the Z performance criterion. A comb generator is used as an artefact and it is moved from one laboratory to another, in order to obtain the measurement results for the final analysis. Suggestions for repeatability improvement are presented. The originality consists of the worldwide program for interlaboratory comparisons started from Continental Automotive Timisoara (Romania). The results presented in this paper continue the work started last year regarding a program for radiated emissions interlaboratory comparison for EMC Laboratories.

articleTitle: Application of Active Learning Methods in the Course "Digital Electronics" in the Topic Digital Comparators Using FPGA Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The application of a laboratory board, based on Spartan-6 FPGA and developed at the University of Ruse, for teaching the courses "Pulse and Digital Devices" and "Digital Circuits" is presented in the paper. The logic blocks in FPGAs are configured to realize complex combinational functions describing the operation of different functional units of combinational type: encoders, decoders, multiplexers, demultiplexers, code converters, digital comparators and various arithmetic circuits. One of the issues considered in the courses is the synthesis and analysis of digital comparators comparing two two-bit or four-bit numbers. Implementing such devices using their schematic presentation and testing them on the board is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of positioning errors for LED
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: We present the research conducted to find what possibilities are to minimize the errors of positioning LEDs, when the LEDs are used as source of light in a measurement instrument. In such a case where the position of the light source enters in computation of the measured value, errors in the LED position are a source of errors for the measurement value. We analyze different types of LED packages and different mounting technologies to find the best way to minimize the positioning errors of the LEDs. We found an important factor that affects the positioning errors indirectly when the light ray is coming out from the LED at a big angle. The refraction of light ray at the package-air interface manifests itself as a position error and should be taken into account because of its magnitude. An effective technique to compensate for the refraction errors that intervene here is to compute in the microcontroller the exact value of the offset produced by the refraction and then subtract that from the position.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Detection and Behaviour Characterization for Video Surveillance Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Nowadays, to identify potentially dangerous situations created by pedestrians, performing video surveillance systems are more than necessary. The application presented in this paper is designed to automatically detect individual pedestrians and analyze and characterize their behavior. Based on this result, an informed security decision can be made. The implementation uses YOLO (You-Only-Look-Once) [1] to detect people in a real-time video stream and evaluates and characterizes their movement, based on data collected from the current video frame and a certain number of past video frames. A series of tests revealed that our system successfully detects both regular and irregular pedestrian trajectory type and also the type of movement: walk, run or stand. The processing speed of up to 77 FPS for YOLOv3-tiny and 21 FPS for YOLOv3 qualifies our solution for real-time operation in a surveillance system, if it is running on a computer platform equipped with a NVIDIA GPU with CUDA capabilities.

articleTitle: An ECG-Based Authentication Scheme for Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Biometrics is the field of identifying subjects based on physiological and behavioral characteristics. Over the past few years, the electrocardiogram signal has become a hot topic in human identity recognition, mainly due to its robustness to attacks, universality and liveness detection. This paper makes use of these properties to generate ECG-based hash codes for inter-sensor authentication in body area networks. Mutual authentication prevents unauthorized access to sensors and actuators. The solution is lightweight and does not require a high computing power, making it perfect for small, wearable or body implanted sensors. Moreover, since only the hash code is transmitted, no sensitive-health related data is exposed. Finally, since the ECG signals used for hash generation are collected from different parts of the same subject, the mechanism is not vulnerable to errors due to physiological and psychological stress.

articleTitle: Software-in-the-Loop System for Motor Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper examines the reliability of the Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) testing environment precisely to test embedded system algorithms. The integrated algorithms system was developed around a BLDC motor based on a real-time operating system. The main features and functions of the control algorithms developed and implemented in an embedded system is to control the BLDC motor speed. The integration of the control algorithms of a BLDC motor model from the Model-in-the-Loop (MiL) process into the SiL process comes precisely from the increasing need to reduce the amount of prototype testing and to check the resistance of control algorithms to conditions errors that are not practical to test on the hardware. To prove the efficiency of the SIL strategy, three types of algorithms have been developed and implemented for controlling such an electric motor by applying optimization techniques based on closed-loop regulators. The code generated after these models is tested and validated through different test scenarios according to the source model, creating a test report after which we can validate the correctness of the code generated in the SiL process.

articleTitle: Embedded RTOS for a Smart RFID Reader
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Location information systems are widespread and the demand for them is growing due to the increasing spread of mobile devices. The information can be used by context-aware systems to provide the user with relevant data corresponding to current actions. In a museum chamber the user can receive detailed information of the surrounding exponents, or when changing the rooms during working hours the office phone can be redirected to the current location. A couple of different location aware infrastructures are available in order to collect position data. Mobile phone towers, GPS satellites, video cameras, badge proximity detectors are just a few of the possible solutions. Through the mentioned sensors, position or proximity information can be obtained. In this paper a system concept based on smart Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) readers will be presented. Through the proposed system location properties will be provided to the context-aware system. Details of the embedded real time operating system of the smart reader will be provided in order to manage the complex protocol of communicating through RFID technology.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Presence Detection System Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The study presents a methodology for detection of pedestrian presence at road crossings. It is based on image processing and a recognition background pattern. For each camera image is applied a filter in order to exclude pedestrians outside the waiting enclosure from affecting the system's decisions. Next, the object is converted to black and white format and is divided into sections. Each section is compared with the corresponding section from the recognition pattern pixel-by-pixel. The relative error between the two images is then compared to a critical value, and a decision is made. The analysis of the images by sections reduces the influence of potential vibrations, thus significantly increasing the probability for correct recognitions.

articleTitle: Setup for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In our days, the humankind is searching for new methods of saving every amount of energy that can be generated by people doing daily activities like walking, driving or exercising. The amount of energy generated by motion for a single person is low, but if we harvest energy from millions of people, we can use that energy to drive low energy consuming devices and save non-renewable resources. A method of saving energy from walking is to develop a piezoelectric system which will be placed in tiles from crowded areas. In this way, the energy created by people doing their daily activities will be harvested and used to power devices like LEDs displays, street lighting or phone charges. The experiment consists of pushing with a force of 800 N (the equivalent force for an 80 kg person) on a piezoelectric energy harvesting system design in a tile form and determine the amount of energy that can be harvested.

articleTitle: Personal Assistant Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents an autonomous device that can be used as personal assistant. The solution consists of a system composed by an autonomous robot, an android application, a web site and a wearable device. By using these components, we can serve multiple purposes depending on the users' needs, thus eliminating the need to buy one device for each function. The hardware components of the system were carefully chosen such as the trade-off between quality and price would have an optimal value: good quality whilst making it affordable to the day-by-day user.

articleTitle: Analysis of activity detection data pre-processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Nowadays collecting sensor data is not just a trend, is a necessity. The increasing occurrence of smart home devices, which are now a permanent part of our homes and life, makes this process of gathering, storing and using this data crucial. One of the most important aspects is data pre-processing, as the process and methods involved must be carefully chosen to obtain the best results. We aim to improve data pre-processing for PIR based activity sensors. Our chosen activity detection system is CASAS, a complete system for detecting and storing activity, where we have access to raw data. The pre-processing is done in MatLab and we tackle the option to divide the main activity into multiple sub-activities or even segment the activity data into suitable windows. After that, we look over the data-labeling and feature selection process. Also, we analyze the possibility of making possible predictions based on existing data.

articleTitle: Influence of Manchester encoding over spreading codes used in multiple access techniques for IoT purposes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for the use of spreading codes in multiple access systems. Such systems have a number of drawbacks, the most important one being that, with the increasing of used code length, the overall system rate increases, so, consequently, the Bit Error Rate (BER) performances at the receiver end might decrease. In order to partially circumvent those disadvantages, we combine the spreading codes with Manchester encoding, avoiding thus the apparition of long sequences of '0' or '1'. Extensive simulations have been performed in Matlab in order to evaluate the BER performances versus Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) for different types of spreading codes used (PN, Gold, Walsh Hadamard), and different modulation techniques (BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM). The results are compared with the standard techniques, without Manchester encoding, and a number of interesting results will be highlighted.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Dye Sensitized Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Photovoltaic energy conversion is today a very hot topic. The technical solutions are already on the market, the silicon crystalline or amorphous being the most used solar cells. We present in the paper investigations on a promising different type of solar cell called Dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC)[1]. This cell presents different construction and operation principles from silicon cells and is presented as a possible solution for large area or flexible panels. We present here electrical measurements on three DSSC prototype samples, compared with a commercial silicon cell, for different illumination levels. The voltage-current characteristics and the main parameters of the cells, as short circuit current, open circuit voltages, maximum power point (MPP) are comparatively presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Design of Regenerative Active Clamping Snubber for a Phase-Shift Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the design process of a regenerative active snubber circuit at the output stage of a phase-shift (PS) converter. This converter topology is popular for high-power domains, having a good efficiency and the advantage of almost no switching losses, fixed frequency operation and soft switching control. However the parasitic capacitance of the transformer and rectifier produces ringing and high overshoot voltage spikes, which causes great stress on the diodes. Conventional resistor-diode-capacitor (RDC) snubber circuits can mitigate this drawback, but they suffer from significant energy losses while existing active snubber circuits often have difficult mathematical models. The novelty of this paper resides in the improved active snubber topology and the detailed, easy to use mathematical model developed for component dimensioning.

articleTitle: Adaptive Learning for Virtual Investigation of Capacitors’ Electrical and Physical Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The article examines a methodological approach for the implementation of adaptive e-learning and studies some physical and electrical parameters of the capacitors. Emphasis is on both structuring of learning content in lessons, in order to achieve adaptability and on creation of computer adaptive classes. We present an opportunity in order to adapt the classes according to the level of the tested student. Design, creation and learning is realized through the online platform Engine for Virtual Electrical Engineering Equipment (EVEEE) for teaching on course "Electrotechnical materials", for the students from bachelor's degree of the University of Ruse.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Domestic Microcontroller Application that Operates with Long Standby Time Intervals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: It is easy to optimize a voltage stabilizer which works in switching mode, when it is used in a power supply circuit for a specified load that operates in permanent mode. A good example is an embedded system with microcontroller. It has many working modes, but in this paper two of them are considered: active (wake) and sleep. The paper is a study of the influence of the coil quality factor under efficiency for the aforementioned modes. It was used a dc-dc converter MC34063 in a domestic automation circuit. In its operation there are shorts intervals of activity interleaved between long standby time intervals (sleep mode). In terms of power consumption, different optimization criteria are formulated for each of the two states. Theoretically, the efficiency is a weighted sum of the efficiency for each state. If the activity time is negligible, the optimization criteria are: the safety of the wake-up and sleep transitions and the energy consumption in sleep mode.

articleTitle: Solar Tracker for Autonomous Power Supplying of Electronic Systems Used in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper is presented the design and the implementation of an enhanced positioning module intended to be used in the implementation of highly efficient solar energy based autonomous power supplying units for electronic systems operating in isolated locations. The targeted application of the system is in the agricultural domain, for powering the electronic equipments that are used in intensive fruit farming systems based on precision agriculture concept. The proposed double axis solar tracker allows an increase of up to 15% in the performances in comparison with a regular photovoltaic system based on fixed mounted panels. The solar tracker is realized using a set of stepper motors that are controlled by a computer through a series of drivers and latches. For an increased flexibility and reliability, the control algorithm for the solar tracker was realized in LabVIEW graphical programming environment.

articleTitle: Polarity Determination of Electrolytic Capacitors in Power Supplies from external terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the extension of the method previously developed, concerning the identification of the correct assembly in an electronic circuit of a polarized capacitor [1]. The method is upgraded to in-circuit testing readiness for switched-mode power supplies and represents an efficient and very low-cost alternative to the "classical" Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) techniques. The charging - discharging technique can be applied to the external terminals of a switched-mode power supply without requiring additional testing points on the electronic assembly.

articleTitle: Investigating the Component Shift during Reflow Soldering at Large Scale Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Component shift or component skewing is a well-known failure for large scale surface mounted (SM) components. The purpose of this paper was to investigate this phenomenon for large scale SMD capacitors with a size of 10 × 9 × 5.5 (lwh) mm. For the investigations, the forces acting on the component were calculated, which included the force due to the surface tension and due to the hydrostatic pressure of the molten solder, the mass of the component and the forces due to the friction. For calculating the forces due to the surface tension and due to the hydrostatic pressure, the shape of the solder fillet was predicted by a geometrical approach. The frictional forces were considered for three boundary conditions as; two states of the solder as being in molten state (viscosity of the molten solder) or in paste form, and besides for the two states of the paste as being fresh (force due to viscosity) or dried out (frictional forces). The non-Newtonian viscosity of the solder pastes was addressed by the Carreau-Yasuda rheological model. Results showed that this type of components can shift even 1 mm in less than 200 ms during the reflow soldering, which may results in open joints and failed circuit. By the results of our analysis regarding the component shift during reflow soldering, the first pass yield of manufacturing, and the quality of assemblies could be enhanced significantly.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic algorithm in autonomous vehicle navigation based on RFID sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The gradual implementation of active safety systems in modern vehicles, through private solutions and those widely accepted by car manufacturers, has several positive effects, from increased passenger and pedestrian safety, to fuel consumption optimization for initial effects of pollution reduction. In the context accelerated deployment of active safety systems techniques, by installing in-vehicle sensors, upgrading road infrastructure to allow for the installation of specific sensors, it is important to establish a common development environment for major automotive manufacturers and research programs.This paper investigates the influence of sensors mounted along a modeled roadway, in a controlled environment, by developing a displacement algorithm through the implementation of a fuzzy logic control system and implementing a recognition and control system based on UHF-RFID technology. Passive RFID tags have been researched and used in transport and control systems but acting as safety beacons. The novelty of this concept is the development of an identification system based on a four-point triangulation through written GPS coordinates on RFID labels thus, real time vehicle identification can be achieved.

articleTitle: Investigating shadowing and possible tombstoning caused by large SMD components during vapour phase reflow soldering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, the tombstoning failure is investigated during heat-level type vapour phase reflow soldering (VPS), where the heat transfer is based on condensation. Different measurements were performed according to different printed circuit board (PCB) test patterns, to investigate possible shadowing caused by larger surface mounted (SMD) components in the close proximity of smaller surface mounted components, pointing to possible tombstoning failures either by condensate congestion or by vapour concentration dynamics. The basic concept was to intercept, whether a large power electronics component would affect the heating on nearby smaller chip-sized resistors, which are susceptible to such problems during VPS. Three test patterns were applied according to different component orientation. Three 0805 and an alternative 0603 component matrix was designed around larger components in the centre on printed circuit boards, where three further setups were investigated: a 4036 large size SMD capacitor, a XAL1010 SMD inductor, and without large SMD, for reference setup. A sweep on the power settings was performed with a heat-level vapour phase soldering oven. Shear strength of the components was also evaluated. It was found that both the shear strength of the components and the occurring tombstone failures of the solder joints are affected rather by paste printing and positioning precision, than any shadowing caused by larger components. The results might be used for further investigations of the tombstone failure during VPS, and during special soldering cases where thermal profiles must be set with unorthodox approaches (e.g. thermally sensitive biodegradables).

articleTitle: Characterization of the V-Model Approach in Thermal Design Process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Thermal management is one of the most challenging fields, especially in case of high-power electronics. In order to foresee and resolve thermal-related challenges in electronic systems, in each stage of the electronic product development, this paper proposes a V-model based approach of the thermal design to ensure proper thermal management. A case-study is presented that covers different stages of the thermal design process of a generic single-phase smart meter used for both indoor and outdoor operations, for which the thermal V-model approach can be applied successfully.

articleTitle: Enhanced Stack-up for EMC, SI and PI in Mixed-Signal Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The stack-up for printed circuit boards is one of the most important factors in defining the performance. In this paper, we proposed a stack-up for a mixed-signal system that caters the problem of EMI suppression, noise, signal and power integrity. The stack-up provides two external controlled impedance layers and one buried controlled impedance layer, which may be used to route one of the power supplies rails for the analog circuits. It also has two ground layers and one layer for power supply rails with an excellent interplane capacitance. Besides this, the stack-up offers a minimum loop area and a minimum power plane noise coupling.

articleTitle: Test Bench for Electrical and Performance Evaluation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are the most used power sources and energy storages currently, being used in the household domain, portable tools, telecommunications, renewable energies, urban mobility and electric cars. Testing plays an important role in the safe use of batteries and to determine a set of criteria that define their performance. A successful battery management relies on protection, in case of both compliant and non-compliant use, on an accurate estimation of the battery's performance parameters to ensure an optimal functioning of the system it is integrated in, but also to prolong and protect the battery. Based on the national and international testing standards for commercial lithium-ion batteries, this paper presents a test bench that includes a set of experimental testing procedures that investigate the electrical abuse and performances of lithium-ion battery cells and battery packs.

articleTitle: Reliability Tests on SAC-xMn Solder Alloys
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Different Sn based micro-alloyed solder alloys with manganese content were developed for the electronic industry as a possible cost-effective candidates. The commonly used SnAg3Cu0.5 (SAC305) lead-free solder alloy applied as a reference. As a first step, various technological parameters tested from the solder alloy-manufacturing point of view. During the reliability investigations of the solder alloys, Vickers hardness, tensile strength and shear force tests were carried out. The results show that Mn content SAC alloys are useful in the electronics technology especially in those fields, where the high reliability is not required.

articleTitle: TIC-TAC Based Live Acoustic Watermarking With Improved Forgery Detection Performances
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Audio recording authentication becomes a necessity as the evolution of technology allowed the manufacturing of small and performant recording devices. The difficulty of editing audio recordings has decreased significantly, given the development of the audio editing software. The paper describes an improved version of a recently proposed live watermarking system based on the TIC-TAC signal. The version presented in this paper eliminates some detection flaws of the original version, studies the effect of the propagation of the original live watermark signal through various acoustic environments, and proposes an improved version that is less affected by those effects.

articleTitle: Thermal Model for LED Luminaire
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Various electrical and thermal models can be found in literature but the thermal models developed for this paper, both the Spice equivalent circuit as well as the SolidWorks thermal simulation were built based on the assumption that there will be two ambient temperatures: one at the heat sink level and a different one above the primary lens of the LED. This difference is due to the fact that the LED is part of a lighting assembly that features a lens/light diffuser that prevents the exchange of fluids between the primary lens of the LED and the exterior of the assembly. In this paper the influence of the two different ambient temperatures on the LED temperature is studied.

articleTitle: Effects of Excitation Waveform on Developing Planar Core Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The development of magnetic materials aimed to work in high frequency domain, became a challenge for the power supply designers who expect to obtain the input/output power ratio near unity. An efficient power conversion process involves the identification and reduction of all the loss sources in the components, either the magnetic or semiconductors. An isolated conversion solution becomes prior to analysis the power transformer. Recently, good enough results were obtained in high frequency approaches regarding the use of planar magnetic components. Losses that involve magnetic cores refer to eddy currents and hysteresis. Available results regarding the core losses in magnetic materials are subject to sine wave excitation. This paper presents a study of core losses obtained for two planar transformers, according to the excitation waveform effects. The approach results become more important taking into consideration that the working frequency is near 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding Radiated Emissions Produced by a Head Up Display
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The radiated emissions (RE) measurement is one of the most important tests that must be performed during a full qualification stage, in order to validate an electronic product for series production, in the automotive industry. Radiated emissions test must ensure that the level of the spurious signals is below a frequency dependent stated value (limit), agreed for proper operation of the DUT in its intended environment and application. The originality of this paper is to present a shielding solution that is confirmed in both near field and far field to reduce the time to market for the product. The magnetic near field measurements are performed by using the EMSCAN system. Acquired near field signals are used for finding the electronic components that are the source of emissions and as guidelines to the solution.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Characteristic Studies of Underwater ROV. ANSYS – Fluent Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper presents the hydrodynamic characteristic of remotely operated underwater vehicle (AUV). Using a AUV model achieved in laboratory of Constanta Maritime University, we study the hydrodynamics of the submarine using simulation to observe the floatability and the motors position. We consider the four forces on the ROV: their own weight, the Archimedes' force, the propulsion of motors and the traction force. Using some simulation, we link the traction force with the speed considering the main direction. According to the fundamental principle of statics, to maintain a constant speed, such as speed maximum, all forces must mutually cancel each other. So by designing according to each vector of the landmark. This paper is focused on how ANSYS-Fluent can point out design problems at the virtual prototype.

articleTitle: Electronic Module for Carbon Monoxide Monitoring and Warning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The IoT domain is in growing exponentially. Monitoring the values collected by sensors, displaying, interpreting and making a decision after analyzing them, are very important steps that are performed within an IoT (Internet of Things) system. At the same time, another important concept is that of energy saving, for example by using energy delivered by photovoltaic panels. Two important parameters to monitor are the level of carbon monoxide and temperature in an enclosed space since high values of these parameters can endanger human life. This project falls within the field of IoT and is based on the concepts described above; the temperature value and the carbon monoxide level are processed by a microcontroller and transmitted to a database, and to a telephone application respectively, in order to be able to permanently monitor their values. If the carbon monoxide level exceeds a certain level, the buzzer associated with the system will alert the people in the room and a supervisor, by means of the Internet connection. In the following chapters the block diagram, together with the main components, the implementation and testing of the system will be presented.

articleTitle: Intelligent monitoring and analysis system of soil moisture parameters and trunk diameter used in fruit tree culture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a solution for monitoring soil moisture parameters and trunk diameter and automatic analysis of their evolution for apple crops. Based on the evolution of the values of these two parameters a determination of the health conditions of the crop is made and then can be elaborated efficient irrigation and fertilization schemes. Identifying the patterns that indicate a certain health state of the fruit tree is done by using a deep neural artificial neural network running on the server where are the data from the monitoring system.

articleTitle: Analysis of RTK Corrections for GNSS Ground Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, we address the position accuracy required in the User Segment. The goal is to find the required minimum distance from the provider receiver to the correction receiver. Several correction receivers, located at different distances, have been used to investigate the accuracy improvements provided to a chosen receiver, which played the role of the user. The applied method reveals valuable findings about the importance of the distance between a reference station and the user. The obtained results can be used to determine the necessary accuracy requirements for different GNSS applications.

articleTitle: A High Detection Rate Pupil Detection Algorithm Based on Contour Circularity Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A pupil detection algorithm that exhibits a high detection rate is presented. This work builds on two previously proposed algorithms and includes a procedure that provides an initial global adaptive threshold that is further adjusted by a feedback loop. The processing steps involve a blurring phase, two morphological operations, contour determination using Laplacian, a convex-hull enclosure as well as a novel contour processing solution that ensures that the contour of maximum circularity is always chosen as the pupil. Finally, the Least Square Fit to Ellipse (LSFE) procedure is used to accurately estimate the position of the pupil center. The proposed algorithm achieves a 95% average detection rate at five pixels for two representative databases.

articleTitle: Design of Solar Monitoring Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The main purpose of the paper is to present a novel idea that is based on design and development of an automatic solar tracker system that tracks the Sun energy for maximum energy output achievement. The proposed system can store the measured data on SD card, and also can visualize the measurements online. The hardware part and programming part have been concurrently developed in order for the solar tracking system to be possible for it to operate accurately.

articleTitle: Method for Detecting Resonance Frequency in Induction Heating Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Induction Heating (IH) Systems use the electromagnetic induction phenomenon for the applications of heating electrically conductive materials, especially metals. In this context, eddy currents are generated within conductive material and its resistance leads to Joule Heating Effect of the object. At the resonance, the equivalent circuit is pure resistive and the power transmission from the inductor to the workpiece is maximum. Therefore, the main purpose of this project is the detecting of the resonance frequency. In this case, it was used a measurement algorithm based on a fixed-point Digital Signal Processor (DSP), member of TI's family C5000<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>, named TMS320C5535. This digital system controls the switch frequency of the transistors from H-Bridge until the phase-shift between output voltage and output current of the resonant circuit is approximately zero.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a power management system with IoT features
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Summary: A low cost integrated power management solution has been implemented to be used in mono-phased powered apartments. For the proposed solution, a household consumption management strategy was developed and then a practical implementation of a system capable of monitoring power consumption and to control the operation of household appliances based on configurations depending on their type, consumption and assigned priority. By its nature, the system also provides power supply protection for over-current or short-circuit by automatically shutting down the power circuits. The system is connected via Wi-Fi to the Internet and it can be controlled in real-time via a webpage.

articleTitle: 2D Virtual Laboratory for Teaching BCD to Seven-Segment Decoders in Logic Design Classes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This study presents the design and development of a virtual laboratory for the Logic design course. A novel implementation of a BCD to seven-segment decoder is shown, which allows student to connect and verify the behavior of the circuit themselves. This is achieved with the use of virtual LED indicators, visualizing the state (digital zero or digital one) of all sockets of the logic gates. Furthermore, a reference BCD to seven-segment decoder is available, allowing students to compare the behavior of the circuit they connected with it. For the above reasons, the presented virtual lab is applicable in traditional, as well as in distant and lifelong education.

articleTitle: The Creation Process of a Secure and Private Mobile Web Browser with no Ads and no Popups
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The aim of this work is to create a new style web browser. The other web browsers can have safety issues and have many ads and popups. The other web browsers can fill up cache with the logging of big history of visited web pages. This app is a light-weight web browser which is both secure and private with no ads and no popups, just the plain Internet shown in full screen. The app does not store all user data, so the navigation of webpages is done in incognito mode. The app was made to open any new HTML5 web page in a secure and private mode with big focus on loading speed of the web pages.

articleTitle: Voltage Software Optimization Control for Constant Frequency Commutation of a BLDC Sensorless Motor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper the authors present an efficient control of the time based commutation sequence of a sensorless brushless direct current (BLDC) motor. The control is achieved using an algorithm commonly used for stepper motors, with a fixed commutation frequency and controlling the supply voltage for the three phase bridge made up of six transistors. Experiments have proven that for a fixed commutation frequency of the command signals, the motor's RPM (rotations per minute) stays constant for a wide range of values of the supply voltage during each of the six steps. Experiments have also revealed that the instantaneous current used by the motor's phases for the same torque has small variations dependent on frequency of commutations that control the motor's RPM. It results from the experiments that when increasing the motor's RPM, the needed current increases following a nonlinear function. This paper proposes a way to generate the minimum supply voltage for the three phase bridge that provides the minimum current needed to generate the engine power. An 8 bit microcontroller based solution is proposed for the theoretical and experimental model.

articleTitle: Developing Software-Based Plug&Play Capabilities for Analog Sensors over a Network Using a Microcontroller Development Board
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The present paper describes a standard C algorithm (mathematical equations + software implementation) for making analog sensors Plug & Play over TCP/IP - Ethernet protocol. This algorithm represents a beginning step for creating a prototype of smart transducer system according to IEEE 1451 family of standards. The sensors are connected to the Analog Input Ports of a microcontroller (MCU) development board. The standard C program running on the microcontroller will automatically detect the connected sensors and will send a list of sensor information over TCP/IP - Ethernet to a remote location. The MCU algorithm is able to detect when a sensor is connected to any of its I/O Analog Ports by monitoring some external and internal parameters like: the default I/O port voltage value, the voltage value of a port when a sensor is connected to that port, the influence between analog ports when connecting a sensor to a port. The microcontroller development board is partially programmed to be an HTML Web Server. In a Web Browser will be displayed the status of all Analog Input Ports. When a sensor is detected, a text file containing sensor data will be created on a local micro-SD card (data logging capabilities). The sensor data can be accessed through a Web Browser by using the IP address of the Web Server.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic based fault detection and diagnosis: an automated design methodology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Fault detection and diagnosis are fundamental steps in maintaining high quality standards in electronic circuits mass production, while keeping the costs at a minimal level. This paper proposes an automated method for designing a fuzzy logic system for the fault detection and fault diagnosis of electronic circuits. Data from the real circuit and from its simulated version is acquired and processed, so that the fuzzy system's rules can be established. The rules model the faulty functioning of the circuit, as well as the fault-free state. The activation degree of each rule will indicate the faulty component. The entire process is automated by means of the MATLAB environment. Tests were carried out on a triangular and rectangular signal generator circuit, assuming the passive components were faulty, and the signals' amplitudes and frequency are the measurements of interest. Based on whether the measured values are low, normal or high, and by means of the fuzzy inference, the system successfully achieves fault detection and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Failure detection on PCBs: an image processing based approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The concern to identify methods to obtain low cost levels in testing printed circuit boards is an important issue in quality assurance. In this paper, a fast and low cost testing system is proposed, based on images captured using optical and thermal cameras. The images are divided into blocks; all blocks are compared with reference blocks provided by reference images. Our system detects the differences and delivers a message with the name of the device or the group of devices that fail. Next, a decision tree is used, to set the trajectory of the tested board.

articleTitle: Analysis of Current Carrying Capability of Graphene-Enhanced Conductive Polylactic Acid Based Filaments for 3D-Printing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents some investigations on the current carrying capabilities of 3D-printed graphene-enhanced conductive poly-lactic acid based samples. Such samples with different dimensions and shapes are tested at different currents and electrical and thermal measurements are performed. An automated measurement system is used for observing any change in sample resistance for the time span of each test. Simple qualitative conclusions modelling and simulation of resistance of 3D-printed samples will be performed and an empirical model for their maximal current capabilities will be identified.

articleTitle: Study of Modification of Conductive Adhesive by Nanoparticles and Aging of Modified Adhesive
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Bonding with electrically conductive adhesives is one way of connecting in modern electronics. In particular, heat-sensitive components are mounted in this way. However, the electrical and mechanical properties of conductive adhesives are worse than those of solders. Therefore, ways to improve these properties are sought. One of them is the modification of adhesives by adding nanoparticles in low concentration. The goal of the work was to find how concentration and quality of mixing the nanoparticles into the adhesive influence the resistance of adhesive joints. It was found that the mixing quality of nanoparticles in the adhesive is of comparable importance to the concentration of these nanoparticles. Then modified adhesives were aged at the high temperature (125°C, 45 % RH) and the high relative humidity (98 % RH, 24°C). It was found that moisture has a significantly greater effect on increase the joint resistance than the temperature. Method of factorial experiments was used for data processing.

articleTitle: Transmission Module with Frequency Hopping for Wireless Sensor Mesh Networks Used in Plant Stress Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper present the results regarding the simulation and the practical implementation of a transmission module based on the principles of frequency hopping spread spectrum technique (FHSS). The module is dedicated for high speed, spectral efficient wireless sensor mesh networks used in plant stress monitoring systems. The proposed design relies on a circuit architecture that uses a set of frequencies that are periodically switched according to a three bit code produced by a pseudorandom generator. The switched frequencies are used as carrier signals for transferring data blocks between the nodes of the mesh network. A critical problem in this approach is represented by the generation and quickly switching, without significant distortions, of a large set of carrier signals, but this problem was alleviated by using a high performance PLL based frequency synthesizer. Compared with other similar implementations the presented solution ensures a communication with increased immunity against noise. Another advantage of the proposed design is represented by the improved energetic efficiency which allows lowering the power consumption of the module due to the operation using the frequency hopping spread spectrum transmission technique.

articleTitle: Smart Monitoring System for Reflow Soldering Equipment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper is presented a smart monitoring system that is able to detect, prior to the periodic maintenance service, a set of malfunctions that may negatively influence the quality of the solder joints on PCB but also the process productivity using a reflow soldering equipment. The proposed smart monitoring system use a vibration and temperature sensor, an industrial controller and a program that offers a real time user interface. The smart monitoring system assures with its capabilities a fast intervention of the process operator in order to eliminate all undesired production problems and to assure the quality of the electronic products. This approach is novel and actual as yet were reported in the last period other kind of improvements for the reflowing process.

articleTitle: Parametric conducted Filter Design for multi-phase DC/DC converters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A method is proposed to design the conducted emission filter for a multi-phase Dc/DC converter on the 48V automotive boardnet.

articleTitle: The performance of an uplink Massive MIMO OFDM-based multiuser system with LDPC coding when using relays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: As our dependency on mobile Internet and mobile phones is increasingly more obvious, the resources of the implemented systems need to support it. In order to achieve that, the fifth generation (5G) standard and future wireless networks are now the main point of interest that can cope with the explosive demand on data traffic, considering the new or the existing technologies that must be reviewed or improved. One is the technology where multiple antennas are used at the receiver/transmitter ends (MIMO) which evolved to Massive MIMO, but with a much higher number of antennas. Another one is the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation technique that brings its benefits by reducing the inter-symbol and intra-symbol interference. Low-density paritycheck (LDPC) codes have capacity-approaching advantage and relatively low and scalable decoding complexity. Cooperative relaying manages the difficult problem of ensuring coverage and capacity at the cell border and it is cost effective. Therefore, in this paper is proposed a Massive multiuser MIMO system with OFDM and LPDC coding when using non-regenerative relays. Further, we are interested in the quality of the information that reaches the base station, considering that only spatial diversity gain is employed, by implementing a minimum mean-square error (MMSE) detector in combination with successive interference cancelation (SIC).

articleTitle: Determining the duration of execution of some functions and alghorithms for the Arduino Uno platform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Determining the execution time of an algorithm that processes real data is very important in many cases. This article proposes a software determination method as well as compensation for certain errors that arise precisely because of the instructions used.

articleTitle: Electrically Conductive Paste Printed Volume Influence on Bonds Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents the investigations of bonds mechanical and electrical properties function of electrically conductive paste printed volumes. For the experiments, it was taken into consideration the SW180 electrically conductive paste type which was used only for bonding chip resistors on the pads of interconnection structure having electroless Nickel immersion Gold (ENIG) finishing. The test vehicles contain a daisy-chain structure with ten 0 Ω resistors, 2512 case. The printed volume was controlled by the stencil thickness (100/150 μm). The mechanical tests (shear test) had been performed at five different temperatures (298/323/348/373/398 K) and they had been completed with electrical measurements and microstructural analysis.

articleTitle: Algorithm and Model for a Fixed Sun Position Detection System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A sun position detection system that is not based on movements made by mechanical components is presented. The proposed solution uses a low-resolution optical sensor as a detection element and a number of optical fibers placed with one end on the surface of a hemisphere and the other in the proximity of the photo sensor serving as solar light guides. The structural arrangement of the fibers maps points on the surface of the sensor hemisphere to points on the optical sensor. Having a well-established correlation between the insertion position of each of the optical fibers on the surface of the dome exposed to sunlight and the area of the photo sensor that each of the optical fibers illuminates, it is possible to determine the position of the Sun on the celestial vault by processing the photo sensor output (by identifying the maximum brightness spots in the resulting grayscale image).

articleTitle: Avoiding Expensive Specialized Equipment in Testing the Stability of a Buck Converter Using Time Domain Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The common way to check converter stability is via frequency domain analysis, by measuring the open loop frequency response, and observing the control loop cross-over frequency and phase margin at the cross-over point. It is a complicated measurement, requiring specialized, expensive equipment and fine skills. A simpler way to quickly check converter stability and performances is via time domain analysis by applying a fast load step to the converter and observing the output voltage response during the load step; It will highlight potential problems regarding loop stability, input supply stability, slope compensation issues, load regulation and layout problems. The electronic load could suffer a hardware simplification too by taking account that it is not necessary usage of an expensive one but an emulated one.

articleTitle: Implementation of a prototype air quality measurement system using MEMS sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of a growing technology, which is micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) sensor technology, with an explicit, complete design and an implementation of a custom prototyping embedded system capable of air quality measurement, hazard detection and other functionalities given by the possibility of attaching additional hardware. Air pollution is becoming a major health problem that affects millions of people worldwide. In support of this observation, the World Health Organization estimates that every year, 2.4 million people die because of the effects of air pollution on health [1]. We have designed the system to be used in the automotive industry, but also to facilitate an easy integration in smart houses and smart factories. It is based on ATmega 2560 microcontroller and combines on a single printed circuit board (PCB) several MEMS sensors capable of measuring the pressure, temperature, humidity, volatile organic compound, carbon dioxide, combustible gas, hydrogen sulfide, nitrogen oxide, smoke and particulate matter. Our system comes to the fore of the future users who might try to get a new perspective on the atmospheric composition in applications such as air pollution management in the city, where the data requirements of the sensor system have not been firmly established yet, and the methods of data collection are still at the beginning. An increase of system functionality can be easily achieved by using additional hardware that can be stack on the main circuit board. In this way, a display is connected to the prototype system in order to view the values in real-time. As a result, we are presenting a system capable of measuring air quality using a trending technology of MEMS, with all sensors directly mounted on the printed circuit board (PCB), with the advantage of fast respond, low price and easy integration with other systems. The experimental results were obtained by developing the module and using it to monitor the air quality in a closed space, inside of a vehicle.

articleTitle: Application of More-level Stress on Conductive Adhesive Joints
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Three types of stresses have sequentially loaded adhesive joints formed of three types of adhesives with isotropic electrical conductivity. One type of the joints has been prepared by mounting of jumpers (0R0 resistors, type 1206) on the test board. For manufacturing these joints adhesives SC 70MN and Permacol 2369/2 have been used. The second type of the joints has been formed by printing of lines from adhesive between neighbouring pads. Adhesive CW 2200 has been used for manufacturing of these joints. The adhesive joints have been first stressed mechanically by deflection of the board with mounted resistors, then by the thermal shocks -40 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C/+80 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C and then at the combined climate 80 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C/80 % RH for 300 hours. Before and after every type of the load the joints resistance has been measured. It has been found that the mechanical stress as well as stress caused by the thermal shocks have had only low influence on the joints resistance. On the other hand, stress in the combined climate temperature/humidity caused significant changes of the joints resistance due to the penetration of water molecules into the adhesive and affecting quality of the insulation barriers between the filler particles.

articleTitle: System on Chip Implementation of a Fuzzy Logic Based Autonomous Robot Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A System on Chip (SoC) implementation of a fuzzy logic sensor fusion architecture for an autonomous robot navigation system is proposed in this work. The core of the system is based on a zero order Takagi Sugeno fuzzy logic controller, whose structure is optimized to benefit from the specific properties of the Zynq-7000 SoC arithmetic DSP48 slices in terms of computational speed and logic resource consumption.

articleTitle: Scaling of Components for Explicit Modelling of Heat Transfer during Vapour Phase Reflow Soldering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper, heat transfer on different surface mounted components is investigated during vapour phase reflow soldering (VPS), where the heat transfer is based on condensation of the heat transfer medium. It is known, that the filmwise condensation differs considerably from more conventional soldering heat transfer mechanisms; our focus was to extend the board level explicit modelling of heat transfer to the range of surface mounted devices (SMDs). The components chosen for investigation ranged from 1206 size to 5040 on the chip-size SMD package scale. Smaller components were omitted from practical reasons. The temperatures of the components were measured with thermocouples lead into the centre. The Biot-numbers for each components were calculated to validate the possibility of explicit modelling. Heat transfer and resulting temperature profiles were calculated according to different modelling approaches. It was found that for smaller components, the modelling approach does not give acceptable precision, however with increasing component dimensions, acceptable results can be achieved.

articleTitle: A System for Measurement of the Asymmetry between Left and Right Shoulders
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The study presents the development of a system for measurement of the asymmetry between the human shoulders. Such measurements are necessary in order to diagnose potential muscular imbalance and when possible, take corrective actions in the form of daily exercises. The system is based on two infrared proximity sensors, installed above the shoulders of the investigated human shoulders. A calibration procedure of the sensors and a following calibration model selection reduced the absolute error for the shoulders difference below 1.49 mm. Yet, if the measurement distance is kept within the range (40...110) mm, the accuracy is below 1 mm.
