The experiments also showed that the calibration is individual for each reflection surface, which should be considered during experimental measurements.

articleTitle: The Generation of Random Numbers Using the Quantum Tunnel Effect in Transistors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper proposes a random number generator based on the quantum tunnel effect that takes place in transistors. The main system is divided into two basic components: the entropy source and the postprocessing block. The quantum tunnel effect is subjected to a random character, which means that electrons have a probability to pass through the potential barrier of the transistor. Theoretically, the measurable output current of the transistor should have a random variance in a predetermined interval, that results into a random sequence. Afterwards, the postprocessing block extracts the bias from the generated array. It is implemented through a hash function which employs the Toeplitz matrix, resulting into a true random sequence. This paper accounts the preliminary stages of development of an original random number generator. The focus was the physical phenomena, the tunnel effect in transistors, and the study of its probability with respect to the device parameters. In terms of postprocessing the main regard was choosing the adequate extraction method for the quantum entropy source. The novelty of the paper is represented by using the tunnel FET as an entropy source and finding a suitable postprocessing model for a higher generation rate.

articleTitle: Controlling the Temperature and Humidity in a Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper presents a solution to control the temperature and humidity in a greenhouse. A previous implementation was based on the exchange of air masses between the interior and exterior of the greenhouse. But it was difficult to obtain a lower and stable inside air temperature than outside. In order to solve this problem, a solution based on water vaporization under high pressure was taken into consideration. The generator of the vapours is driven by an automated controller which measures the temperature and humidity inside the greenhouse. Yet, the solution has a drawback: because the vapour condenses on the leaf, there is a risk of infection. In order to prevent it a specific sensor for detecting the leaf wetness is used. Fans and curtains could be also used if necessary. The solution is an extension of the previous application and assures a more accurate environment for the optimal plant growth less affected by the outside weather conditions.

articleTitle: Intrusions and Their Lock in Data Communications Through Internet
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Intrusions on entities in a network can be manifested by: identity theft, fraudulent routing, target flooding with protocol messages, and broadcasting an ICMP protocol messaging protocol. Intruders lead to blocking the service for legitimate users, and targets are flooded with unsolicited emails, Protection against such actions can be done with a number of security measures, such as: installing firewalls and installing intrusion detection systems. These safeguards can eliminate or even minimize the likelihood of materializing security threats and prevent attacks on the security features of a system.

articleTitle: Monitoring Current Variation using Pattern Recognition Algorithm Implemented in Automotive DC Driving Servomechanism
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In this paper the authors consider the problem monitoring of the drawn current by the main power rail that powers multiple consumers (servomechanisms, actuators, electromagnets, stepper or DC motors) present in cars, in order to protect the equipment present on board a car or to increase the reliability of electromechanical systems. The idea is to scan the supply current of a device connected to the main power rail using a very sensitive shunt and to store this data using a development board with a microcontroller and implementing maps of the currents that will be supplied to specific consumers. The board operates in two stages. The first stage involves memorizing the shape currents and storing the data in a memory zone. The second stage assists the current utilization of the equipment by using a software block to recognize the shape of the current. Recognition of the current shape and classification of the current event into nominal or faulty operation will be done using byte oriented comparisons initially and using a variable error filter afterwards using "running average" which will be presented below. Preliminary results were done on a 16-bit microcontroller.

articleTitle: Digital Processing Method used to Improve the Frequency Measurement Accuracy for Vibrating-Wire Transducers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper is focused on implementation of a digital processing method applied over acquired data obtained from a vibrating wire transducer in normal conditions. The paper carries on the researches from [2] and [3], the main aim being to improve measurement accuracy of transducers with natural frequency around 700Hz. The theoretical analysis of the vibrating wire transducer shows that the output signal is a sum of harmonics: fundamental ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> (natural frequency of the vibrating wire) and higher frequency harmonics ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>. But a FFT analysis of the transducer's output signal shows that, inside the working range, the output signal is strongly affected by noise and that the second degree harmonic is nearly to the high frequency limit. The conditioning circuit studied in [2]-[3] can't extract just fundamental frequency ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>. To improve circuit performance this paper proposes to use digital processing methods. Theoretically, the transducer's output is a damped oscillations signal, but from processing method point of view this is viewed like a series of numbers represented by the samples of signal periods of oscillation acquired as long as the output signal is higher as a threshold. In our work, the high frequency noises are rejected with low pass FIR filter and the 50Hz noises are rejected using an averaging operator. As a results of the processing, the fundamental frequency is measured with an accuracy less of 0.2Hz.

articleTitle: New Laboratory Concept Used with the Data Acquisition System Fundamentals Course
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The paper analyses a new lab concept, in all its aspects: the method, the flow, the instruments, the platform, the requirements and the results. Theory, simulation, hands-on experiment and verification concur and confirm each other. However, differences between theoretical equations, simulation model analysis and experimental measurements are emphasized. Multisim SW was used for editing and simulating the schematics, Ultiboard for layout, "Analog Discovery" workbench and WaveForms SW are used for measurements and functional analysis. Three years of conducting the new lab demonstrate a better implication of both students and instructors. The success encourages students to extend the experiments beyond the lab handout required exercises. Despite a higher challenge for both parties, the increase of the satisfaction level and the measurable student's results confirm the success of the new concept.

articleTitle: Determination of deformations in PCB using tensometric stamps
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: When I made a study on the structural deformation of a building's steel, I came up with the idea of using this method also for the deformations that can occur in printed wiring. In the case of buildings, it was the action of an external force applied to that structure and affecting different parts of that structure. In the case of the printed wiring, these external forces may also act to modify the shape of the PCB by modifying its flatness to tear. The problem that arises is related to the positioning of the sensor. The sensor used is 120-ohm resistive tensometric stamps, and the method of measuring and determining the action of a force I will describing in this paper.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scheduling for an Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper proposes a real-time energy management system for a smart microgrid with renewable energy resources. The basic components of the microgrid are a biomass generator, a geothermal generator, and several photovoltaic modules. Moreover, a battery bank is also available to store the excess generated energy or to ensure that the energy deficit is covered. The purpose of this algorithm is to determine the optimal operating points of the generators, to ensure a minimal energy waste and to save costs. The optimal scheduling strategy is based on the mixed-integer linear programming algorithm and a communication protocol interpreter implemented using an RS-485 network. Furthermore, it is considering the impact of uncertainties in solar PV, and load forecasts.

articleTitle: Triaxial Vibrating – Wire Transducer Implementation and Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This article wants to reveal a step-by-step mounting and measurement procedure of a dam-dedicated sensor and to reveal the importance of a potential comparative analysis between two measurement methods used in the process of following the behavior of the hydro- technical constructions. When dealing with sensors mounted in dams, tunnels or inside mountain galleries it is very important to have an additional method, redundant with the manual old one. Two historical measurement sets were acquired and compared using a built-in interface: the first being the result of the data manually introduced by the technicians that are responsible with the measurement (with the help of a caliper) and the second being the result of the data acquired using an automated equipment installed.

articleTitle: Study of biofilm evolution using a monitoring water system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Simulation of waterfall in nature can be done using a fluid level control system in a pool. This system is made of two mini-pools at a height of 50 cm from each other. The water monitoring system consists of a control and control board that reads the temperature and the flow rate of the water and pumps the water from the lower container to the top. In the pools are introduced different types of substrate (e.g. naval steel, liquid wood) that simulate the resistance of materials in contact with sea water and the evolution of biofouling formation on these materials. The aim of the project is to detect the appearance of biofilm layers on the materials that are integrated into a ship's body, during the time. A comparative analysis is presented in this paper for different type of material and different environmental condition.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Boolean Functions Using Decoders and Logic Gates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A laboratory board based on Spartan-6 FPGA is created at the University of Ruse and it is intended for teaching the courses "Digital Circuits" and "Pulse and Digital Devices", introducing the students of the electrical specialties to the main topics of digital electronics. Based on configuring the logic blocks in FPGAs complex Boolean functions are performed. In these courses students study how to build a circuit using logic gates (for example, only 2-input NAND logic gates) or using some functional units of combinational type: decoders and multiplexers. One of the topics covered in the courses is the synthesis and analysis of devices implementing given Boolean functions using decoders (or a cascade of decoders) and logic gates. Implementing different Boolean functions using their schematic presentation and testing it on the board is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Education 4.0 – Jump to Innovation with IoT in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) will play a key role in Higher Education. Our contribution leads the road to innovation within IoT for Education 4.0, using a system comprising smartwatch data, health data, learning analytics and Artificial Intelligence. By using embedded sensors from wearable devices, we can add value to Education 4.0. Smartwatches are IoT devices, equipped with a multitude of embedded sensors collecting distraction-free huge amounts of real-time data during students' learning. In our paper we highlight advantages of wrist-based wearables like smartwatches for Education 4.0. We develop a User Experience Questionnaire for the measurement of acceptance of advanced electronic technology in Higher Education. We identify as experiment's results the most important sensors and protocols for Education 4.0.

articleTitle: Enabling IoT in Education 4.0 with BioSensors from Wearables and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: A major challenge for Education 4.0 is to make use of wearable devices for helping students in monitoring their learning behavior and their activities (steps, heart rate variability, and heart rate) in real-time. The first aim of this paper is to present our implementation of adaptivity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods within the Education 4.0 process. In this work, we investigate embedded biosensors (noninvasive, low-cost, and distraction-free) used in smartphones and smartwatches. The next objective is to enable IoT for Higher Education, i.e. a novel system assisted by AI that takes embedded biosensor data and environmental data into account in order to estimate students' wellbeing and health. In this regard, we propose a framework that uses wearable devices to collect data with biofeedback methods to support students' academic success.

articleTitle: Humidity Sensing System Using Plastic Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: In the current paper we proposed a new method to measure humidity by means of the transmission losses occurring through an uncoated optical fiber. The measuring principle behind this method was developed and tested in a small-scale laboratory environment. A standard system for measuring air humidity was necessary as a reference, so an NTC temperature measurement component was used to fulfil this requirement. The whole system is characterized by simplicity, since most of the others employ complicated chemical deposition processes.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Wireless Sensor Nodes with Augmented Reality Application Support
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Nodes are currently used in fields such as industrial automation, Internet-of-Things, smart marketing, and even medicine, where they are implanted in living organisms. In order to remove all the hassles and design challenges of a battery powered device, the paper proposes an ultra-low power wireless nodes system that can be sustained with thermal energy harvesting alone. Combined with an Augmented Reality application, it is a self-sustainable, eco-friendly and intuitive way of gathering data without requiring maintenance or human intervention. A minimal footprint prototype is presented, along with the steps taken to keep the average current consumption to a minimum while fully maintaining system functionality: dynamically updating connection parameters as required, and optimizing the software running on the Wireless Sensor Nodes. The results of this research are sustained by the simulations, measurements and tests presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Skin Anomaly Detection Using Classification Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for the most easily detectable type of cancer, skin cancer. Due to the ozone layer thinning, it was observed an increase in the number of skin lesion anomalies. Those anomalies are produced by the increasing UV radiation intensity. Good protection against sun is not always facile, mainly in the exposed regions of the skin like the face and the lower regions of the arms. Most types of cancers can be easily extracted via surgery if they are detected in one of the incipient development stages. Using a high resolution image, a classification algorithm can detect certain patterns in the nevi color, shape, veins or irregularities inside. Analyzing those aspects, a person can track their nevi development easily and intervene if it necessary. The originality of this paper consist in designing several convolutional neural networks, using the Python programming language, the Keras API and the Tensorflow framework alongside with proper dataset selection. The convolutional neural networks were trained using an open source dataset, with the purpose of formulating a diagnosis for new patients. The convolutional neural networks are provided with 7 classes of images, representing 7 types of skin lesions as input, and will output a diagnosis. The result of the research was a classifier with a convenient classification accuracy based on the dataset, and a medium accuracy based on new data.

articleTitle: A Gradient-based Sensitivity Analysis Method for Complex Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: Most sensitivity analysis methods from literature impose specific experiment plans (design-of-experiments). Moreover, the size of the experiment plan, which is in conjunction with the number of system evaluations, increases with the number of factors that may affect the systems' behavior. This paper introduces a gradient-based global sensitivity analysis method which overcomes these limitations. First, its performance is compared against six sensitivity analysis methods on sets of polynomial test functions. The comparison is carried out by means of the number of system evaluations implied and the reported factor ranking list. The proposed method proved to have comparable accuracy to the best of the six known methods- the EFAST method- with the advantage of a lower number of system evaluations. These two methods are further applied on an electronic system, an E-Bike application. In this case, the proposed method employs the verification plan of the EFAST method, as well as a standard Monte Carlo experiment plan with about one third of the system evaluations of the EFAST. Even with a much lower number of system evaluations, the proposed method yields the same result as the EFAST method in terms of the factor ranking list.

articleTitle: Development of a Thermal Camera Using a Low Noise High Speed Far Infrared Camera
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 25th International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a thermal imaging camera using a low noise high speed far infrared sensor from Melexis, MLX90621, and integrating it into an embedded solution alongside a microcontroller from STMicroelectronics with an ARM processor, a 1.8" TFT liquid crystal display and various other peripherals, all powered from a Li-Po battery whose voltage is regulated using a buck-boost converter. The main application of this device is inspecting assembled PCBs for thermal faults, although it can be used for other purposes such as non-contact temperature measurements, automotive thermal comfort system, intrusion detection.
